data.name: So Long Earth
data.detailed_description:
So Long Earth é um jogo casual focado em puzzles e aventura e conta a história de um protagonista mal humorado e da sua nova vida fora da Terra.
Haverá horas de exploração por todo o universo enquanto tu desvendas a história de Dominique juntamente com o seu minion.
Se gostas de um jogo simples que podes simplesmente ligar, sentares-te numa cadeira com um comando e relaxar, então este é o jogo perfeito para ti.

data.short_description: So Long Earth é um jogo de ação, plataforma e puzzle feito para contar a história de Dominique Fayar, um membro da máfia francesa que encontrou refúgio no espaço depois de a Terra ter sido destruída.

reviews.review:
So Long Earth is an unusual science-fiction puzzle platformer that embraces a small-scale, casual approach instead of attempting to deliver an enormous space epic. Developed and published by Ed Farage, it places players in the role of Dominique Fayar, a French mafia member who manages to escape Earth shortly before the planet is destroyed. It is an eccentric starting point that immediately separates the adventure from more conventional stories about astronauts, soldiers, or heroic explorers. Dominique is not exactly humanity's ideal representative, and that unconventional personality gives the journey much of its character.

Gameplay revolves around a combination of platforming, exploration, puzzles, and relatively light action. The mechanics are intentionally approachable, making the game more suitable for players interested in progressing through environments and discovering what comes next than those searching for punishing platforming challenges. Obstacles and puzzles provide structure to the journey without overwhelming the experience with complicated systems. This simplicity makes it easy to understand, although it can also leave the gameplay feeling limited for anyone accustomed to platformers built around advanced movement mechanics or demanding puzzle design.

Exploration plays an important role because Dominique's journey is not simply about surviving after Earth's destruction. Traveling through the universe gradually reveals more about his background and circumstances, giving players a reason to continue beyond completing individual platforming sections. His minion accompanies him on the adventure, adding another quirky element to a story that rarely takes the traditional route. The contrast between the catastrophic destruction of an entire planet and the strangely personal story of a disgruntled mafia survivor helps establish the game's distinctive sense of humor and identity.

The overall pacing is deliberately relaxed. So Long Earth is the type of experience that can be played casually rather than requiring players to memorize complicated mechanics or constantly perfect their reactions. Controller support complements this straightforward design and makes the platforming comfortable to approach. The downside is that players expecting intense action, complex combat, or increasingly elaborate mechanical challenges may find the experience lacking in depth. Its strongest appeal lies in the combination of simplicity and eccentricity rather than technical mastery.

Visually and technically, the game reflects the modest scope of an independent project. It does not depend on elaborate graphics to communicate its ideas, instead relying on its science-fiction environments, characters, and unusual premise to establish atmosphere. Its extremely modest hardware requirements also make it accessible on older computers. The installation footprint is very small, further emphasizing that this is a compact production rather than a large-scale adventure filled with cinematic presentation and highly detailed environments.

There is nevertheless a respectable collection of supporting features. The game includes 60 Steam achievements, Steam Trading Cards, Steam Cloud functionality, controller support, and a selection of language options. It is primarily designed as a single-player experience, so the focus remains firmly on Dominique's personal journey. The large number of achievements can also provide additional objectives for players who enjoy completing smaller challenges and pursuing full completion after experiencing the main adventure.

Steam Deck compatibility is reasonably encouraging, although the experience should not be confused with full Steam Deck verification. The game is considered Playable on the handheld rather than Verified. It can operate on SteamOS with suitable performance, and its interface text is generally usable on the smaller screen. However, certain interactions may require touchscreen input, the virtual keyboard, or adjustments to the controller configuration. Players can also encounter controller prompts that do not perfectly correspond to Steam Deck controls, while display settings may require some manual attention. It is therefore practical for portable play, but users should expect occasional configuration or input inconveniences.

As a free-to-play title, So Long Earth is easier to recommend as an experimental indie experience because there is little barrier to discovering whether its unusual style works for you. Its limitations become noticeable through its simple mechanics and modest production values, but there is also something appealing about a game willing to build a space adventure around such an unlikely protagonist. It does not need dozens of complicated systems to establish an identity, and the combination of exploration, puzzles, platforming, humor, and narrative discovery gives it enough variety to remain interesting for players who appreciate smaller independent projects.

Ultimately, So Long Earth succeeds more through personality than mechanical sophistication. Its strange premise, accessible gameplay, relaxed pacing, and compact presentation create an experience that is easy to pick up but unlikely to satisfy players seeking a deep or highly challenging platformer. Dominique's journey provides the adventure with an eccentric charm, while the science-fiction setting gives its straightforward mechanics a broader sense of discovery. It is best approached as a curious and lightweight indie adventure that offers a few hours of exploration rather than a major genre-defining experience.

Rating: 6/10
